raw_segments.text: I, if the population continues to double every twenty-two years, as it has done for the last
two hundred years, the number of inhabitants in the United States in 1852 will be twenty
millions, in 1874 forty-eight millions, and in 1896 ninety-six millions.
This may still be the case even if the lands on the western slope of the Rocky Mountains
should be found to be unfit for cultivation.
The territory which is already occupied can easily contain this number of inhabitants.
One hundred millions of men disseminated over the surface of the twenty-four states, and
the three dependencies which constitute the union would only give seven hundred sixty-two
This would be far below the mean population of France, which is one thousand sixty-three
to the Square League, or of England, which is one thousand four hundred fifty-seven.
And it would even be below the population of Switzerland, for that country, notwithstanding
its lakes and mountains, contains seven hundred eighty-three inhabitants to the Square League.
See, Malt Brun, Vol. Roman VI, P. 92.
